entities.name: Domnall Ua Lochlainn
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Domnall Ua Lochlainn, also known as Domhnall Mac Lochlainn (d. 1121), reigned as King of Ailech and over-king of the Cenél Eógain from 1083, asserting a powerful claim to the High Kingship of Ireland for nearly four decades. As a scion of the Northern Uí Néill, his rule represented a resurgence of their traditional dynastic authority, challenging the dominance of the Uí Briain of Munster and shaping the complex political landscape of 12th-century Ireland. His reign was characterized by relentless military campaigns and astute political maneuvering, aimed at consolidating his authority in Ulster and beyond, making him a pivotal figure in the last decades of a truly native Irish high kingship.

Throughout his extensive reign, Domnall engaged in a prolonged and often brutal rivalry with Muirchertach Ua Briain, King of Munster, for supremacy over Ireland. Major confrontations included the decisive Battle of Magh Coba in 1103, where Domnall's forces inflicted a significant defeat on the Uí Briain, and numerous 'circuits' of Ireland (tours intended to enforce submission) by both contenders. Despite never achieving undisputed recognition as High King 'with opposition' in the annals, Domnall's consistent military strength and his ability to repeatedly compel submission from provincial kings across the north and east underscore his formidable power. He also patronized ecclesiastical reform, notably attending the Synod of Ráth Breasail in 1111, which established the diocesan structure of the Irish church.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Domnall Ua Lochlainn's nearly four-decade reign as King of Ailech and claimant to the High Kingship significantly shaped the political landscape of pre-Norman Ireland, preventing the Uí Briain from achieving undisputed national dominance and solidifying the power of the Cenél Eógain in Ulster.
